findings.title: Validation ignores the resolved worktree
findings.description: `resolveProjectWorktree` can return a `worktreeId`, but this action discards it and always validates against `project.projectPath`. When run from a separate registered worktree, explicit paths are resolved from that worktree’s CWD but are outside the main project’s document root, so they are silently skipped; a run without paths scans the main checkout instead. This can make a validation gate report clean without checking the worktree’s changes. Resolve and validate the worktree path, or reject that context explicitly, and add coverage for worktree invocations.

findings.title: A later date backfill can undo the fix run’s timestamp
findings.description: Fixes are applied in finding order. For a document missing both a fixable field such as `status` and `dateUpdated`, the first write stamps `dateUpdated` with the run date. The later `dateUpdated` finding writes the original `dateCreated` value; the writer intentionally skips stamping when the field being updated is `dateUpdated`. The command can therefore exit successfully after modifying the document while leaving a stale `dateUpdated`. Apply date backfills before other fixes, or otherwise ensure a document changed by the run retains the run’s date; add a regression test for multiple findings on one file.

findings.title: Every action error is reported as an invocation error
findings.description: The action catch calls `handleError(err, 2)` for every error, not just project-resolution or configuration errors. Unexpected failures—for example, a storage read error—therefore receive exit code 2, although the documented contract reserves 2 for invocation errors. Distinguish expected invocation errors from operational failures and test both exit-code paths.

findings.title: The docType test does not test the rejection it claims
findings.description: The test is named as though a wrong `docType` is caught, but its `devlog` and `gate-evidence` values are valid registered types, and it expects an unregistered type to produce no findings. The validator selects a schema using `data.docType` and skips validating that field’s values, so these assertions do not demonstrate rejection of a mismatch. Rename the test to describe the pass-through behavior, or add a meaningful mismatch case if rejection is intended.
